observations: body L1-L2, L13: the dashes after «b)», «I.» and «II.» measure 10.1, 10.3 and 10.4 pt; the dash after «cursum ».» (L2) measures 9.5 pt and follows the full stop without a space.
body L2: the full stop after «l» of «l: 11» prints as a colon, two dots one above the other; kept as printed.

body L3-L9: «Platone Atheniensi», «Ptolemaeo», «Schiaparelli», «Hultzsch», «Pauly» and «Wissowa» are letter-spaced; the dashes of «Pauly–» (L8) and «Real–Encyclopädie» (L9) measure 5.3 pt each. The Greek is set as printed: ἰσοδρόμοι ἡλίῳ and περὶ αὐτὸν ἀεὶ φερόμενοι.
body L10: «al–Qazwīnī» is letter-spaced, its long dash joined to the Q.
body L12: the Arabic «يدور حول الشمس», ‘revolves about the Sun’, follows «revolvi» within the quotation.

body L13-L16: «Ibn Yūnus» and «Caussin» are letter-spaced in L13, «Ibn Yūnus» not in L16; «al–Battānī» (L14) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.3 pt), and so is the dash of «115–16» (L15, 5.2 pt). «a quae» (L16), for «ab iis quae», as printed.
body L18-L20: the head of the chapter is set in the larger type, as printed. The dash after «a)» measures 9.7 pt and the hyphen of «28-29» 3.5 pt. In L20 «planetarum» is upright, as printed.

body L21-L32: «al–Battānī» (L21) and «Ptolemaeus» (L25) are letter-spaced; «al–Battānī» (L32) is not. The rule of the translation, p. 117, l. 31-38, compares the times of rising or setting, at the latitude of the place, of the degrees of the ecliptic that rise or set with the planet and with the Sun: arcs of the equator, as L21 says, but oblique ascensions, where L22 names right ascension. At the beginning of Cancer the arcs of right ascension exceed the corresponding arcs of the ecliptic in the ratio 1 : cos ε, 1.09 with al-Battānī's obliquity 23° 35′: Saturn's 14° of the ecliptic, taken equally on both sides of the solstice, are 15° 16′ of right ascension, Mercury's 11° 30′ are 12° 32′.

body L26-L29: Ptolemy's arcs are al-Battānī's (translation, p. 117, l. 29-30): 12° ½ + ¼ = 12° 45′, 14° ½ = 14° 30′, 5° ⅔ = 5° 40′, 11° ½ = 11° 30′. The Greek is set as printed: περί, ὡς ἐπίπαν, ἀνατέλλει. The dash of «418–19» measures 5.3 pt.

notes_left L1-L7: «Caussin» is letter-spaced. The Arabic is «جهة», ‘side, direction’, and «في جهة», ‘in the side (of)’. The l of «Halma» (L5) prints broken, like «Ha!ma»; «420-2» has a hyphen (3.1 pt). «necessaria» (L7), for «necessariam», as printed.

notes_right L1-L3: Ptolemy's least depressions of the Sun for the heliacal phases (Almagest XIII, 7) are Saturn 11°, Jupiter 10°, Mars 11° ½, Venus 5°, Mercury 10°, as printed here (notes_left L8 and these lines). «Wolf» is letter-spaced; «1890-93» and «423-24» have hyphens (3.2 pt each). The rule between the two columns of the notes prints faint and broken.
